Reloading a window, opening another folder or opening a second window to the same host no longer logs in again, so it costs **no MFA prompt** (e.g. no extra Duo push from `ForceCommand login_duo`).

The extension now keeps the SSH connection, the running server and the tunnel to it in a small background process on your computer. A window that reloads attaches to it in a fraction of a second, without opening an SSH session on the server.

### Install
Close the editor, then:
- Linux / macOS: `curl -fsSLO https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GuyliandeJong/oneshot-remote-ssh/main/install/install.sh && bash install.sh`
- Windows: download `install/install.ps1` and run `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1`

Upgrading from 1.0.0 needs no setting changes.

### Added
- background SSH connection, on by default (`remote.SSH.persistentConnection`). It closes 10 minutes after the last window using it (`remote.SSH.persistentConnectionIdleTimeout`, in seconds), when the network drops, or on **OneShot SSH: Close Background SSH Connections**. The next connection after that logs in again (one prompt)
- command **OneShot SSH: Close Background SSH Connections**

### Changed
- the README links to the [getting started guide](https://github.com/GuyliandeJong/oneshot-remote-ssh/blob/main/docs/getting-started.md)

**Note:** while the background connection is open, any program running as your user can use it, like an OpenSSH `ControlMaster` socket. Set `"remote.SSH.persistentConnection": false` to connect from each window as before. Hosts that use GSSAPI authentication always connect from the window.
